description: Declaration-only F5 behavior for the PULP APB I2C: the same level interrupt and trigger as pulp_i2c_level_f5.json, but the acknowledge is stated as an ordered three-step clear_sequence (acknowledge write, status read, release write). The declaration normalizes; this host performs one clear write and refuses the sequence by name.
notes: apb_i2c.sv:128 states `wire iack = r_cmd[0]` and apb_i2c.sv:189-193 `irq_flag <= (s_done | i2c_al | irq_flag) & ~iack`: CMD[0]=1 is the held acknowledge that clears irq_flag, and a second CMD write releases it so the peripheral is not left masking later transfers. A device whose acknowledge is really two register writes and one register read is stated as what it is here
the read step is the handler's status observation (STATUS at offset 12), which is not a write and therefore is not something the current handler can perform as part of its clear sequence

this file is not referenced by a runnable scenario. The executor's own scenario key (irq_clear_sequence, up to two writes) is a different declaration that the host does execute; the behavior schema states the general form and refuses what it cannot run, by name
no execution is claimed for this file
